images.filename: Torpedo damage plan of USS Helena (CL-50) in the Battle of Kuly Gulf, 6 July 1943 (C l5001).jpg
images.caption: Torpedo damage of the U.S. Navy light cruiser USS Helena (CL-50) in the Battle of Kuly Gulf on 6 July 1943. The bow broke off after the first hit. Minutes later two torpedoes hit amidships after which the ship jacknifed.

images.caption: Japanese destroyer Tanikaze drydocked in Yokosuka shortly after the battle of Midway. Coming under attack from B-17 bombers and carrier aircraft, dozens of bombs were thrown at Tanikaze, but through excellent maneuverability, she was not directly hit by a single bomb. Near miss damage did shred her bow, as photographed, sending her into repair. Tanikaze later served in the battle of Kula Gulf, where she helped to sink the light cruiser USS Helena (CL-50) and was torpedoed and sunk by the submarine USS Harder (SS-257) on 9 June 1944.

images.caption: A view of the Japanese fleet anchored in Staring Bay taken from the floatplane of the heavy cruiser Atago. Several Japanese ships are labeled, including the aircraft carriers Akagi and Kaga, the battleships Kongo, Hiei, and Kirishima, the heavy cruisers Takao, Atago, Tone, and Chikuma, and the light cruiser Abukuma. The four destroyers of desdiv 17 (Urakaze, Isokaze, Tanikaze, and Hamakaze) are seen anchored ahead of Abukuma, as are several support ships.
